title.narrative: Orange Gem Project – Empowering Women through Production of Orange-fleshed Sweet Potatoes in Plateau

description.narrative:
Nigeria produces an estimated 3.9m MT of sweet potatoes annually making it the largest producer in West Africa, and among the top five producers globally . Sweet potatoes can be produced in all of Nigeria’s 36 states, however Plateau state in north-central Nigeria accounts for 80% - 90% of Nigeria’s potato production, including sweet potatoes. Although yet to be a staple food in Nigeria, there is a growing demand for orange-flesh sweet potatoes that current supply is not able to meet. The Orange Gem project aims to increase the incomes of women producers in Plateau state through the regenerative cultivation and sales of OFS potato vines while also increasing awareness on the benefits and versatility of OFS potatoes.
The project will adopt an integrated approach in line with the Nigeria country program. Given the focus on women, and the geographic focus in Bokkos and Barkin Ladi LGAs, which are conflict prone regions in Plateau state, the Orange Gem project will also mainstream messages on women participation in peacebuilding and gender justice. As a conflict-prone region, the low nutritious level of women and children is exacerbated underscoring the significance of the Orange Gem project in also promoting better nutrition and increased livelihoods among women.
